chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the sacrificial offering: what may be eaten from it? He said: Every offering that is due to a deficiency in the hajj, then do not eat from it; and every offering that is part of the completion of the hajj, then eat.

key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial offering presented in connection with hajj
key_terms.تَمَامِ الْحَجِّ: the completion or proper fulfillment of the hajj rites
key_terms.فَلَا تَأْكُلْ: then do not eat from it
key_terms.نُقْصَانِ الْحَجِّ: a deficiency or shortcoming in the hajj requiring compensation

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim eat from the hajj sacrificial offering if it was required due to a deficiency in the pilgrimage?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal distinction regarding the hajj sacrificial offering. If the offering is required because of a deficiency or shortcoming in the hajj rites, one should not eat from it; but if it is offered as part of completing the hajj, one may eat from it.
